jobs.title: Plant Manager - Net Zero Modular Construction
jobs.descriptionHtml:
ABOUT US

Reframe Systems is a Physical AI and robotics company on a mission to make high-performance housing attainable and abundant in the communities where people want to live. Through our vertically integrated delivery model and highly automated microfactories, we deliver climate-resilient homes and buildings with greater speed and predictability than traditional construction.

Our volumetric modular buildings are produced in our Andover, MA microfactory, with a growing pipeline across North America and a new microfactory on the way. We are building a system that balances repeatability with site-responsive design, enabling homes adaptable to each site, community, and customer need. Our cross-disciplinary team brings together architecture, robotics, design engineering, software, factory operations, and field delivery to change how housing gets delivered.

We’re reimagining the future of housing through a smarter and more sustainable system that empowers people to live better. Come build it with us.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for a Plant Manager to run the floor of our microfactory and own the daily execution that turns our production plan into finished homes. This is the person the build team looks to every day, the one who holds the line between what the company has committed to and what actually gets built on the floor.

We are at a scaling inflection. Over the next year we move from our prototype facility in Andover to a 100,000 square foot factory in Billerica, grow direct labor from around 20 to 80 or more, and step up output from roughly 10 homes in the last year to 40 to 50 in the next, on a path to far higher volume after that. We need an operator who has built and run a production floor through exactly this kind of ramp, and who runs toward a floor that is short a leader rather than away from it.

This is a hands-on, on-the-floor role. You own daily production, the people who build, and the operating rhythm that keeps quality, safety, and schedule on track. Your job is to run a floor that performs today and gets more capable every week.

You report to the Head of Operations. Until that role is filled, you report to a member of Reframe's executive team.

RESPONSIBLITIES

Production and Floor Leadership

  • Own daily production on the floor: hit the weekly build plan, keep modules moving on takt, and clear the constraints that slow the line.

  • Lead the floor's full production team, including the production managers, area managers, and leads, and be the single point of leadership the team relies on day to day so that no one person on the floor is a single point of failure.

  • Run the daily management system: morning huddles, tiered check-ins, and visual management the team actually understands and owns.

  • Hold area and team leads accountable to weekly targets that step down along the efficiency glidepath, and give them the support to hit them.

Throughput, Quality, and Safety

  • Drive throughput toward our targets and improve labor efficiency by working the lowest-performing processes first.

  • Deliver a quality product. Own the in-process and line checks, catch and correct defects on the floor, and build every module to standard.

  • Lead safety on the floor day to day. Run safety walks, close out action items, and build a culture where working safely is how the floor operates.

  • Own schedule reliability and on-time module completion for active projects.

People and Team Development

  • Build the supervision and shift structure the floor needs as the team grows from around 20 to 80 or more.

  • Recruit, onboard, and develop builders and leads, and grow technicians into leaders the way good operators do, through real scope and candid feedback.

  • Partner with HR and Recruiting on the high-volume hourly hiring and onboarding the ramp requires.

  • Set clear expectations and a floor culture that takes pride in what it ships.

Factory Launch and Scale-Up

  • Help stand up the Billerica facility, from floor layout and work cell design through commissioning and first article, and lead the production team through the move.

  • Establish the daily operating system at the new facility so it performs from the start rather than relearning what we already know.

  • Translate the production plan into staffing, training, and floor readiness on an accelerated timeline.

Systems and Continuous Improvement

  • Be a power user and requirements partner for our internal factory software team. You set the floor's requirements and you live in the tools every day.

  • Run standard work and continuous improvement on the floor, and partner with our operational excellence function to make the factory more capable every week.

  • Manage from the data the floor generates. If it is not measured, it is not managed.

30 / 90 / 1 Year Outcomes

First 30 days

  • Build trust with the production team and current floor leads. Spend most of your time on the floor, not in a conference room.

  • Learn current-state performance (throughput, labor efficiency, quality escapes, safety, schedule reliability) and name the top three constraints holding back the build plan.

  • Re-establish a daily operating rhythm the team owns: a huddle that works, clear daily targets, and visual management people actually use.

  • Get smart on the Billerica move and what has to be true on the floor for a clean ramp.

First 90 days

  • Deliver a measurable lift on the top constraint (cycle time, labor minutes per square foot, quality escapes, or schedule adherence) with a repeatable mechanism behind it.

  • Run a stable tiered daily management system and weekly target reviews that step down along the glidepath.

  • Produce a floor-readiness plan for Billerica in partnership with Manufacturing: layout, work cells, staffing, training, and commissioning sequence with clear dates.

  • Stand up the day-to-day quality and safety routines that scale with a growing hourly workforce.

First year

  • Run a floor that hits its weekly build plan predictably, with throughput, quality, and labor efficiency trending the right way and a supervision structure that holds under load.

  • Lead the production team through the Billerica launch and ramp to stable output at the new facility.

  • Reduce the floor's reliance on heroics and on any single person, with leads who can run their own areas and a growing bench behind them.

  • Deliver a clear step-change in floor performance (cost per unit down, on-time completion up, escapes down) that supports the company's volume and unit-economics goals.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • 7+ years in manufacturing operations, including running a production floor through a real ramp or facility launch, with direct labor reporting to you.

  • You have built a floor from a low base: stood up work cells, supervision structure, and a daily operating system where they did not exist.

  • Strong people leadership, with a track record of growing builders and technicians into leads and holding a team to targets without losing them.

  • Comfort with high-mix, project-based production where the bill of materials and the work move with each job.

  • A real floor presence. You earn trust by being on the floor and solving problems, not by managing from a distance.

  • Strong data orientation and comfort in a technology-forward factory where software is part of how work gets managed.

Nice to Have

  • Experience taking a production operation from low rate to high volume.

  • Construction, modular, or other high-variability production background. Strong manufacturing operators from other industries translate well.

  • Familiarity with lean and TWI, and comfort running standard work and continuous improvement on the floor.

  • Experience setting requirements for and partnering with an in-house software or MES team.

  • You have lived the prototype-to-production transition and know what breaks.

Reframe Systems is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you believe you have the skills to thrive in this role, we encourage you to apply—even if you don't meet 100% of the listed requirements. At this time, we are only considering candidates who are authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future visa sponsorship.

No third-party recruiters or agencies.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We are seeking a Carpenter to join our factory team, contributing to the production of high-quality modular housing components. This role will require generalist skills across framing, finish carpentry, and installation tasks, with a focus on precision, efficiency, and teamwork. The ideal candidate is experienced in carpentry, adaptable, and motivated by a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

RESPONSIBILITES

  • Perform general carpentry tasks, including framing, sheathing, and installation of walls, floors, and ceilings.

  • Assemble and install cabinetry, doors, windows, and trim details in modules.

  • Read and interpret shop drawings, blueprints, and digital plans.

  • Use hand and power tools to execute tasks with precision and consistency.

  • Conduct quality checks to ensure all work meets company standards.

  • Collaborate with other carpenters and trades to complete assigned tasks on time.

  • Communicate effectively with supervisors and team members to resolve issues.

  • Assist with moving materials and organizing workstations to ensure smooth production flow.

  • Ensure proper storage and handling of carpentry tools and materials.

  • Follow all safety protocols and maintain a clean, organized workspace.

  • Conduct routine maintenance on carpentry tools and equipment as needed.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • High school diploma or equivalent.

  • 3+ years of carpentry experience

  • Proficiency in using hand tools, power tools, and measuring instruments.

  • Strong understanding of carpentry principles, including framing and finishing techniques.

  • Ability to read and interpret blueprints and shop drawings.

  • Physical ability to perform tasks, including lifting up to 50 pounds, standing, and working overhead for extended periods.

  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing high-quality work.

WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Factory environment with exposure to construction materials, tools, and equipment.

  • Physical tasks including standing, lifting, and moving materials.

  • Some overtime or weekend work may be required based on production schedules.

WHY JOIN US

At Reframe Systems, you’ll be part of a team that is transforming housing construction. You’ll have the opportunity to contribute to an innovative manufacturing process and help solve critical challenges in housing and climate. We value teamwork, craftsmanship, and the pursuit of excellence.

ABOUT US

Reframe Systems is a Physical AI and robotics company on a mission to make high-performance housing attainable and abundant in the communities where people want to live. Through our vertically integrated delivery model and highly automated microfactories, we deliver climate-resilient homes and buildings with greater speed and predictability than traditional construction.

We are building a system that balances repeatability with site-responsive design, enabling homes adaptable to each site, community, and customer need. Our cross-disciplinary team brings together architecture, robotics, design engineering, software, factory operations, and field delivery to change how housing gets delivered.

We’re reimagining the future of housing through a smarter and more sustainable system that empowers people to live better. Come build it with us.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

We are seeking a skilled Drywall Hanger to join our factory team and play a critical role in producing high-quality modular housing components. This role is responsible for measuring, cutting, and securely fastening drywall panels to wall and ceiling framing in a controlled manufacturing environment. The ideal candidate has strong experience hanging drywall efficiently and accurately, with a commitment to tight seams, clean cuts, and production-grade quality.

RESPONSIBILTIES

  • Measure, mark, and cut drywall panels to fit walls, ceilings, and openings around windows, doors, outlets, and other penetrations.

  • Lift, position, and securely fasten drywall panels to wood or metal framing using screw guns, ensuring proper fastener spacing and depth.

  • Stagger and align seams to minimize finishing work and maximize structural integrity.

  • Install drywall on ceilings using lifts or with a partner, maintaining level and plumb surfaces.

  • Cut openings accurately for electrical boxes, HVAC penetrations, plumbing, and fixtures.

  • Inspect framing prior to hanging to identify issues that would affect fit or finish, and flag them to supervisors.

  • Verify panel selection (thickness, fire-rated, moisture-resistant, sound-rated) matches specifications for each application.

  • Collaborate with framers, finishers, and other trades to maintain production schedules and handoff standards.

  • Communicate with supervisors to address challenges and improve workflow.

  • Follow safety protocols and maintain a clean, organized work environment.

  • Clean, maintain, and properly store tools and equipment.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • High school diploma or equivalent.

  • 3+ years of experience hanging drywall, preferably in manufacturing or construction.

  • Proficiency with measuring, cutting, and fastening techniques that produce tight seams and minimize finishing rework.

  • Familiarity with tools and equipment used in drywall hanging (e.g., screw guns, utility knives, rasps, T-squares, routers, drywall lifts).

  • Ability to read and interpret construction drawings and specifications.

  • Physical ability to perform tasks, including lifting up to 50 pounds (including sheets of drywall), and working overhead or on ladders for extended periods.

  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to craftsmanship.

WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Factory environment with exposure to construction materials, tools, and equipment.

  • Physical tasks, including standing, lifting, and performing repetitive movements.

  • Some overtime or weekend work may be required based on production schedules.

Reframe Systems is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you believe you have the skills to thrive in this role, we encourage you to apply—even if you don't meet 100% of the listed requirements. At this time, we are only considering candidates who are authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future visa sponsorship.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
ABOUT US

Reframe Systems is a Physical AI and robotics company on a mission to make high-performance housing attainable and abundant in the communities where people want to live. Through our vertically integrated delivery model and highly automated microfactories, we deliver climate resilient homes and buildings with greater speed and predictability than traditional construction.

Our volumetric modular buildings are produced in our Andover, MA microfactory, with a growing pipeline across North America and a new microfactory on the way. We are building a system that balances repeatability with site-responsive design, enabling homes that are adaptable to each site, community, and customer need. Our cross-disciplinary team brings together architecture, robotics, design engineering, software, factory operations, and field delivery to change how housing gets delivered.

We're reimagining the future of housing through a smarter and more sustainable system that empowers people to live better. Come build it with us.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to rethink how a construction project gets managed from inception to build.

Construction runs on handoffs: a project moves from a customer conversation to a scope, to an estimate, to a set of purchase orders, to a production schedule, with someone at every one of those boundaries re-entering what the last person already wrote down. The industry has long treated that as the cost of doing business, even though it is where schedules slip, where margin quietly disappears, and why almost nobody in this field can tell you what a building will cost until it is nearly built.

As a vertically integrated company, we are building the opposite of that, which means one authoritative representation of a project that everything downstream reads from, so that sales, estimating, procurement, and the factory all work off the same source of truth and a change in one place propagates. You will work closely with the design automation platform, which turns a building design into a manufacturable model and production plan, and the factory software team, to integrate real manufacturing data into our upstream models. This is part of the flywheel that will truly make construction faster and more predictable: real production data, cycle times, quantities, and labor we actually see on the floor, feeding back into how the next project is scoped, estimated, and bought, so that every building we deliver makes the next one more accurate to plan.

This is a hands-on role to deliver a software experience end-to-end, from understanding the problem statement to designing and deploying a solution. Your customers are the estimators, buyers, and project teams working alongside you, and you would spend real time with them, becoming an expert in their workflows. If you like taking an ambiguous, high-stakes part of a business and turning it into software that people run on, there is a lot of ground here.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own how a project flows through our systems, from the first customer conversation through to what the factory builds, including every handoff in between.

  • Design the underlying data model and system of record, so that each function works from one authoritative representation of a project rather than maintaining its own copy.

  • Build full-stack applications that turn manual, document-driven processes into software that operations teams run their day on.

  • Define the data contracts and interfaces between business functions, and keep them clear enough that engineers and agents can both work against them.

  • Apply AI to the manual and unstructured parts of the process, and build it to drive value in production not just demo well.

  • Partner with other software teams to close the loop between what we plan and what we actually produce, so that real operating data improves the next project.

  • Set the technical direction for how these systems evolve, including where we build and where we buy.

  • Partner directly with the teams who will use what you build to find the highest-leverage problem to solve next, then cut scope until it ships.

  • Mentor and grow other team members; this is an opportunity to shape the software engineering culture in a small, agile team.

QUALIFICATIONS

Prior knowledge or experience in construction or manufacturing is not required. We'll get you up to speed.

Must Have

  • Bachelor's in computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • 7+ years building production software.

  • Strong full-stack engineering, ideally in Python and Typescript, including automated testing, CI/CD, monitoring and alerting, and root cause analysis. You've owned systems end to end, from data model through interface.

  • A track record of gathering your own requirements and owning problems end to end, working directly with the people who will use what you build and turning vague operational complaints into scoped work that shipped.

  • Experience building internal tools for non-technical operators, with at least one you can point to that got adopted and stayed adopted.

  • Comfort with data modeling, pipelines, and warehouse work, without needing to be a pure data engineer.

  • Experience with cloud-native architecture and containerized deployments.

  • Experience using coding agents to prototype, reach a solution quickly, and augment day-to-day development.

  • Comfort shipping across organizational boundaries, into systems and teams you don't control.

Nice to Have

Any of these would be a bonus, but none are required to be a strong candidate:

  • Experience building software next to physical operations: manufacturing, construction, logistics, hardware, or field service.

  • Depth in one or more of estimating and CPQ, ERP or MRP systems, procurement and supply chain software, or PLM.

  • Experience integrating with, extending, or replacing an ERP.

  • Work on a digital thread or similar end-to-end traceability program.

  • Front-end depth, particularly data-dense interfaces for operational users.

  • Deep cross-functional collaboration skills.

If you believe you have the skills to thrive in this role, we encourage you to apply, even if you don't meet 100% of the listed requirements. At this time, we are only considering candidates who are authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future visa sponsorship.

THE ROLE

We’re hiring a Construction Materials Procurement & Supply Chain Lead to own the flow of materials from design decision to installation, across both the factory and the field.

This is a player–coach role. You will roll up your sleeves to run a lot of the day‑to‑day work (RFQs, POs, expedites, supplier management) for active single- and multi-family residential projects. In parallel, design the simple, reliable procurement and inventory system that future projects and factories can run on.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Make sure materials never stall the schedule

    • Own material availability for both factory and jobsite, from permit set through installation.

    • Build and run a clear playbook for long‑lead items so projects are not delayed by materials.

    • Reduce stockouts in kitting and on the floor by setting and managing min/max levels and reorder logic for stocked parts.

  • Build the procurement & inventory “operating system”

    • Turn today’s bill of materials, purchase logs, and ad‑hoc processes into a documented, teachable process that goes from permit set → BOM → RFQs → POs → receiving → kitting → project closeout.

    • Consult with software and finance teams on our bill of materials and materials data standards: part numbering, stock vs off‑the‑shelf rules, and how BOMs must be structured to be procurable and traceable.

    • Stand up a simple but robust inventory tracking approach using Google Sheets + QuickBooks + existing tools, and use it as the basis for future ERP / WMS requirements.

  • Lead supplier strategy for construction materials

    • Source and manage suppliers for structural lumber, sheathing, windows, doors, cabinets, MEP equipment, finishes, and other construction materials – for both factory and field.

    • Negotiate pricing, terms, and programs; launch 2–3 strategic supplier relationships in high‑impact categories (e.g., windows, cabinets, structural lumber).

    • Decide when to buy‑to‑job versus buy‑to‑stock, balancing cash, space, and risk.

  • Be embedded with designers, engineers, and operations

    • Work closely with cross-functional teams to connect material choices to cost, lead‑time, installation effort, and supply‑risk.

    • Propose and analyze material alternatives and supplier options; co‑decide on changes that affect building systems, permitting, or installation.

    • Partner with Factory Operations, Production, and Site Operations to ensure material plans actually work on the floor and on site.

  • Shape our future systems

    • Translate real‑world workflows into clear requirements for a future ERP / WMS, in partnership with Software Teams and Finance.

    • Act as the primary operational stakeholder when we evaluate and implement more advanced systems in the next 1–2 years.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN YOUR FIRST YEAR

  • Projects hit key milestones without material‑driven delays.

  • A working procurement + inventory playbook is in place and used by the team.

  • We have a clear, accurate view of inventory and material spend that can be used in internal reviews and board discussions.

  • At least 2–3 strategic supplier programs are live with measurable improvements in cost, lead‑time, or reliability.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 7–12+ years in supply chain, procurement, or inventory roles in:

    • Construction, modular/off‑site construction, building products, or adjacent manufacturing.

  • You’ve been both:

    • The person doing the work – running RFQs, placing POs, managing suppliers, fixing stockouts.

    • The person designing or significantly upgrading the processes and data structures behind that work.

  • You’ve lived through at least one ERP / WMS implementation or major upgrade as the operations or supply‑chain lead customer.

  • You are comfortable starting with scrappy tools (Sheets, QuickBooks, basic databases) and using them to design the next level of system, not the other way around.

  • You like writing things down: checklists, runbooks, processes, and standards that others can follow.

  • You collaborate well with:

    • Designers and engineers who care about performance and constructability.

    • Factory and field leaders who care about throughput and predictability.

    • Finance and Tech teams who need clear, specific requirements.

BONUS IF YOU HAVE:

  • Experience in volumetric modular, panelized building, or factory‑based construction.

  • Familiarity with light‑wood framing, building envelope systems, and MEP equipment.

  • Experience with project‑based costing and connecting material usage to project economics.

  • Prior work in a startup or high‑growth environment where you had to build systems while delivering against live projects.


Reframe Systems is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you believe you have the skills to thrive in this role, we encourage you to apply—even if you don't meet 100% of the listed requirements. At this time, we are only considering candidates who are authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future visa sponsorship.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
ABOUT US

We’re reimagining the future of housing through a smarter and more sustainable system that empowers people to live better. Come build it with us.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own the structural system for our platform

    • Define standard structural assemblies for walls, floors, roofs, stairs, and connections that balance strength, stiffness, cost, and manufacturability.

    • Set design rules, load paths, typical details, and tolerances that can be reused across products and projects.

  • Bridge design, modeling, and manufacturing

    • Partner with architects and modelers to translate architectural intent into structurally rational, factory‑buildable systems.

    • Work with our Onshape Modeling / FeatureScript teams so structural rules are encoded in models, automation, and shop documentation (not just in isolated details).

  • Lead structural engineering on key projects

    • Develop internal structural schemes and calculations for priority projects before they go to the Engineer of Record.

    • Prepare clear, well‑structured packages for external structural engineers and third‑party inspectors, and drive efficient review cycles.

  • Tighten the loop between design, factory, and field

    • Diagnose structural root causes behind issues like cracking, misfits, or tolerance clashes in factory and field.

    • Turn lessons learned from the floor and jobsite into updated details, standards, and rules that prevent recurrence.

  • Manage and level‑up external partners

    • Coordinate with EORs and other consultants to align on performance criteria, details, and assumptions.

    • Push for designs that are safe and code‑compliant without unnecessary over‑design, and quantify trade‑offs in cost and manufacturability.

  • Contribute to platform‑level system studies

    • Co‑lead investigations into new structural concepts and their implications for cost, throughput, carbon, and field performance.

    • Work with systems and MEP engineering to rationalize penetrations, chases, and integrated assemblies.

  • Prototype automated structural optimization workflows

    • Work with modeling and software teams to design simple, repeatable optimization studies for key framing systems (for example: minimizing steel tonnage subject to drift limits, or comparing lateral systems across cost and constructability).

    • Help define how structural models, analysis tools, and modeling pipeline should interact so these studies can eventually be run automatically for both platforms and projects.

OUTCOMES

By your 90‑day mark, we’ll look to you to have driven tangible, system‑level progress. Specifically, you will:

  1. Establish a baseline structural “kit of parts”

    • Document standard wall, floor, and roof assemblies (including spans, sheathing patterns, shear wall strategy, tie‑downs, and typical connections) for a selected product line (e.g., Triple Decker or comparable module set).

    • Identify where current details are over‑designed, under‑specified, or misaligned with factory reality, and propose targeted updates.

  2. Close at least two recurring structural pain loops between design and factory

    • Partner with factory, modeling, and design teams to select two recurring issues with structural implications (for example: cracking during lifts, truss dimension mismatches, missing shear/nailing schedules, or wall fit problems).

    • For each, deliver:

      • A concise root‑cause write‑up, including structural and process contributors.

      • A concrete change to details, standards, or tolerances that is implemented in our drawings, models, or Sidekick documentation.

  3. Define a repeatable collaboration model with our structural EOR

    • For at least one active project, lead the structural engagement with the EOR from internal concept through stamped package.

    • Produce a lightweight “playbook” for how we want to work with stamping engineers going forward (what we own, what they own, how we avoid unnecessary over‑design, and how we keep decisions synchronized with our models).

  4. Embed structural logic in our digital toolchain

    • Work with modeling and software partners to get at least one important structural rule (for example: standard nailing schedule behavior, span checks, or connection rules) expressed in a way that can be encoded in our parametric modeling workflows.

    • Document the next 3–5 candidate rules that should follow, with a clear sense of impact and implementation difficulty.

  5. Create a shared, practical definition of “structurally done”

    • Align with architecture, modeling, and factory engineering on what “structurally done” means at each stage (concept, permit, issued‑for‑modeling, issued‑for‑factory, issued‑for‑field).

    • Propose a simple checklist or gate for at least one stage that we begin piloting on live work.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience

    • 7+ years of structural engineering experience on building projects, ideally including multifamily or high‑repeatability housing types.

    • Experience with modular, offsite, panelized, or other prefabricated systems is a strong plus.

    • Demonstrated track record of coordinating with architects, MEP engineers, fabricators, and field teams.

  • Technical depth

    • Strong grasp of structural behavior in wood/light‑gauge and mixed‑material systems (gravity, lateral, connections, deflection, movement, and creep).
      Solid understanding of current building codes and standards, including IBC, ASCE 7, and relevant material-specific codes.

    • Familiarity with Massachusetts and/or California building codes, and comfort working with third‑party modular inspection agencies and local AHJs.

    • Proficiency with structural analysis and documentation tools; comfortable working from and back into Revit, and able to collaborate effectively with parametric CAD environments (Onshape, SolidWorks, Tekla, etc.).

    • Experience with or strong interest in API‑driven structural tools (for example SkyCiv, Dlubal RFEM 6, or similar), or a track record of using scripting/automation around more traditional tools (e.g., RISA, ETABS, SAP) to run repeatable studies and optimizations.

  • Systems mindset

    • Excited to turn one‑off project details into reusable patterns and rules.

    • Able to weigh cost, manufacturability, throughput, and embodied carbon alongside pure structural performance.

  • Collaboration and communication

    • Clear communicator who can explain structural trade‑offs to architects, modelers, factory leaders, and executives.

    • Comfortable engaging directly with trades and factory operators to understand what actually happens on the floor and in the field.

  • Bias to action

    • Inclined to test ideas quickly on real problems, including prototypes, then codify what works.

    • Comfortable operating in ambiguity and helping define processes, not just following them.

If you’re excited by the idea of owning the structural backbone of a new kind of housing platform, and you want to see your work move from model to robot to home in weeks, not years, we’d love to talk.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

This is not a role for someone who wants to supervise a steady-state line. We are building the infrastructure to scale, and we need leaders who can bring rigor, systems thinking, and a technology-forward mindset to a genuinely novel manufacturing challenge.

RESPONSIBILTIES

Daily Management & Execution

  • Own daily/weekly plan attainment for your area: throughput, minutes/SF, schedule attainment, and rework hours

  • Run start-of-shift and end-of-shift routines; ensure the team always knows the plan, priorities, and constraints

  • Coordinate labor, materials, and readiness so work is staged and flow is protected

  • Surface blockers early with clear options and tradeoffs (bring “2–3 ways to solve it,” not just problems)

Safety, Quality & Standards

  • Own safety performance for your area: hazard escalation, audits, incident response, and corrective actions

  • Ensure adherence to SOPs / standard work and quality gates; stop and correct out-of-standard work

  • Partner with Ops Engineering / training owners to ensure training and certification are completed for tasks performed in the area

People Leadership & Crew Development

  • Lead, coach, and develop team leads and operators; set expectations and drive accountability

  • Address issues directly and respectfully; hold the line on standards

  • Implement a lightweight rotation / cross-training plan that grows versatility and reduces burnout

Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement

  • Partner with Ops Engineering / CI to identify, prioritize, and execute improvements that move throughput/efficiency metrics

  • Support kaizen events, time studies, and standardization; ensure impact is measured and captured (not just ideas generated)

  • Convert recurring issues into standard work, training content, and improved material flow so the system becomes self-improving

Metrics, Visibility & Systems (“Scoreboard”)

  • Own the area “scoreboard”: targets vs actuals, downtime/constraints, quality escapes, and improvement actions

  • Participate in weekly leads/metrics reviews; report what happened, why, what changed, and what support you need

  • Partner with Factory Orchestration / Sidekick stakeholders to improve dashboards and information displays when current metrics don’t drive behavior

  • Strong people leadership: coaching, conflict management, accountability, and performance conversations

  • Strong data orientation: you run a scoreboard, identify gaps, and drive actions to close them

  • Ability to operate in ambiguity and build structure where it doesn’t exist yet

  • Clear communicator who can escalate issues with crisp context and options

  • Experience with Lean / TWI / continuous improvement systems (daily management, standard work, 5S, kaizen)

  • Experience building training and certification programs (“train the trainer,” sign-offs, skills matrices)

  • Familiarity with tech-enabled operations (digital work instructions, dashboards, workflow tools)

  • Construction / building experience (prefab/modular, wood framing, MEP, finishes, installation sequencing); helpful but not required

  • Experienced Area Manager / Supervisor from a high-velocity factory or fulfillment environment who can quickly learn the “product” (homes/modules)

  • Lead / foreperson from prefab/modular or construction who has already adopted a metrics-driven daily management system (targets, standard work, CI cadence)

  • Establish baseline area performance (throughput, minutes/SF, quality escapes/rework, safety, schedule reliability) and identify the top 3 constraints

  • Stand up or tighten daily management: pre-shift planning, visual management, end-of-shift learning loop, and clear escalation paths

  • Define the area scoreboard (targets vs actuals) and ensure it is visible and used consistently

First 90 days

  • Deliver measurable performance lift against the primary constraint (cycle time, labor efficiency, quality escapes, or schedule attainment) with a repeatable CI mechanism behind it

  • Implement a stable cross-training/rotation cadence that reduces single points of failure and burnout

  • Improve standard work adherence and quality gating so repeat issues begin to decline

  • Establish a reliable weekly cadence for reporting metrics, actions, and improvement progress

First year

  • Your area consistently hits predictable throughput and efficiency with strong safety and quality performance

  • The area runs a durable operating system (tiered daily management + CI cadence) that continues to improve without heroics

  • Training/certification and standard work are mature enough to support hiring ramps and scaling to additional facilities

ABOUT US

Our cross-disciplinary team brings together architecture, robotics, design engineering, software, factory operations, and field delivery to change how housing gets delivered.

We’re reimagining the future of housing through a smarter and more sustainable system that empowers people to live better. Come build it with us.

THE ROLE

Every Reframe project travels from architectural intent, through a detailed 3D model, to work instructions on the factory floor, to modules set on a foundation. The DFMA Project Engineer is the person who makes sure what we design is what our factory can build, and that the people building it have everything they need.

You will be embedded with our Design Engineering team and own buildability for your projects from early design through module release and field set. You bring real construction knowledge into the room when design decisions are being made, map the build information into our models alongside our modelers, and stand behind every module released to the floor. This is a hybrid role: part builder, part engineer, part translator. You will spend time at a desk in the model, in design reviews with architects, and on the factory floor and project sites with your tools.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

During design (SD/DD)

  • Evaluate horizontal and vertical assemblies for compliance with our automation systems, cost, and shape the factory vs. field split for each project

  • Participate in recurring per-project DFMA reviews and weekly engineering calls, flagging design decisions that degrade manufacturability before they become expensive

  • Represent buildability at the table with architects and consultants, drawing on established building system standards

During modeling and module release

  • Work with Design Engineering to ensure the model reflects build reality: design intent, structural drawings, and the way the floor actually works

  • Map build and process information into the model: assigning parts to the right kits, panels, and processes, and defining what each process requires for operators to execute

  • Review production plans, assembly views, and release readiness for every module before it hits the floor

  • Create handoff documentation for every new material, process, or strategy, and develop shop drawings for new processes

On the floor and in the field

  • Diagnose and resolve floor issues raised in end-of-shift debriefs: tolerance stackups, integration speed, framing quality, alignment

  • Build project-specific mockups and first articles before design lock

  • Brief factory and field leads on what changed from the last project and the unique details to watch for

  • Author set instructions and provide hands-on support during set and button-up

  • Translate manufacturer instructions into floor-ready processes for specified products

  • Convert factory and site pain into feedback that improves our projects and standards

WHO YOU ARE

  • A hands-on building background: carpentry, framing, residential or commercial construction, with exposure to MEP trades a strong plus

  • Able to fluently read architectural and structural drawing sets and spot what won't work before it's framed

  • Comfortable in a CAD or BIM environment (Revit, Onshape, or similar), or motivated to become proficient; we will not ask you to be an expert modeler, but you will work inside the model

  • Experience in a factory, shop, or prefab environment a plus

  • A clear communicator who can move between architects, engineers, and builders and be trusted by all three

  • Organized and follow-through oriented: you close loops, document decisions, and don't let details fall between meetings

WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

The gap between a beautiful drawing set and a module rolling off the line is where construction projects go to die. You are the person who closes that gap. As Reframe scales from one project at a time to a portfolio, the engineers in this role are how our build knowledge shows up on every project, every module, every time.

This is not a role for someone who wants to supervise a steady-state line. We are building the infrastructure to scale, and we need leaders who can bring rigor, systems thinking, and a technology-forward mindset to a genuinely novel manufacturing challenge.

 

RESPONSIBILTIES

Daily Management & Execution

  • Own daily/weekly plan attainment for your area: throughput, minutes/ft², schedule attainment, and rework hours

  • Run start-of-shift and end-of-shift routines; ensure the team always knows the plan, priorities, and constraints

  • Coordinate labor, materials, and readiness so work is staged and flow is protected

  • Surface blockers early with clear options and tradeoffs (bring “2–3 ways to solve it,” not just problems)

Safety, Quality & Standards

  • Own safety performance for your area: hazard escalation, audits, incident response, and corrective actions

  • Ensure adherence to SOPs / standard work and quality gates; stop and correct out-of-standard work

  • Partner with Ops Engineering / training owners to ensure training and certification are completed for tasks performed in the area

People Leadership & Crew Development

  • Lead, coach, and develop team leads and operators; set expectations and drive accountability

  • Address issues directly and respectfully; hold the line on standards

  • Implement a lightweight rotation / cross-training plan that grows versatility and reduces burnout

Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement

  • Partner with Ops Engineering / CI to identify, prioritize, and execute improvements that move throughput/efficiency metrics

  • Support kaizen events, time studies, and standardization; ensure impact is measured and captured (not just ideas generated)

  • Convert recurring issues into standard work, training content, and improved material flow so the system becomes self-improving

Metrics, Visibility & Systems (“Scoreboard”)

  • Own the area “scoreboard”: targets vs actuals, downtime/constraints, quality escapes, and improvement actions

  • Participate in weekly leads/metrics reviews; report what happened, why, what changed, and what support you need

  • Partner with Factory Orchestration / Sidekick stakeholders to improve dashboards and information displays when current metrics don’t drive behavior

     

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3–7+ years leading teams in a fast-paced operations environment, with a strong preference for manufacturing / production / fulfillment / industrial operations

  • Proven track record hitting output targets while maintaining safety and quality

  • Strong people leadership: coaching, conflict management, accountability, and performance conversations

  • Strong data orientation: you run a scoreboard, identify gaps, and drive actions to close them

  • Ability to operate in ambiguity and build structure where it doesn’t exist yet

  • Clear communicator who can escalate issues with crisp context and options

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Lean / TWI / continuous improvement systems (daily management, standard work, 5S, kaizen)

  • Experience building training and certification programs (“train the trainer,” sign-offs, skills matrices)

  • Familiarity with tech-enabled operations (digital work instructions, dashboards, workflow tools)

  • Construction / building experience (prefab/modular, wood framing, MEP, finishes, installation sequencing); helpful but not required

Ideal candidate profiles (examples)

  • Experienced Foreperson / Supervisor from a high-velocity factory or fulfillment environment who can quickly learn the “product” (homes/modules)

  • Lead / Foreperson from prefab/modular or construction who has already adopted a metrics-driven daily management system (targets, standard work, CI cadence)

First 30 days

  • Build trust and operating rhythm with Production, Ops Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing and adjacent area leaders

  • Stand up or tighten daily management: pre-shift planning, visual management, end-of-shift learning loop, and clear escalation paths

  • Define the area scoreboard (targets vs actuals) and ensure it is visible and used consistently

First 90 days

  • Deliver measurable performance lift against the primary constraint (cycle time, labor efficiency, quality escapes, or schedule attainment) with a repeatable CI mechanism behind it

  • Implement a stable cross-training/rotation cadence that reduces single points of failure and burnout

  • Improve standard work adherence and quality gating so repeat issues begin to decline

  • Establish a reliable weekly cadence for reporting metrics, actions, and improvement progress

First year

  • Your area consistently hits predictable throughput and efficiency with strong safety and quality performance

  • The area runs a durable operating system (tiered daily management + CI cadence) that continues to improve without heroics

  • Training/certification and standard work are mature enough to support hiring ramps and scaling to additional facilities

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for a Machine Shop & Lab Manager to own FAB1's machine shop, a fully equipped space with mills, lathes, laser cutters, welding equipment, and 3D printers that supports engineering and prototyping across the company. This is a hands-on, full-time role for someone who wants a shop to actually be theirs: maintaining the equipment, running point on tooling and consumables, and building a real training program so employees across the company can get certified on machines safely and confidently.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own the Space: Be the single point of accountability for the machine shop and lab — layout, organization, cleanliness, and day-to-day operations.

  • Maintain the Equipment: Run preventive maintenance schedules, troubleshoot and repair machine issues, and manage relationships with service vendors and suppliers.

  • Manage Tooling and Consumables: Track inventory, reorder consumables before they run out, and make purchasing decisions on new tooling and equipment.

  • Formalize Training and Access: Help build structured trainings so employees can safely get checked out on mills, lathes, laser cutters, welding, 3D printing, and other equipment. Define who's allowed to use what, and enforce it.

  • Set the Safety Standard: Establish and enforce shop safety protocols — PPE requirements, machine-specific safety procedures, emergency procedures — and keep the space compliant and audit-ready.

  • Make the Shop Accessible: Act as the go-to resource for anyone in the company who wants to use the space, from experienced engineers to first-timers, and remove the friction that currently keeps people out.

  • Support Projects: Develop functional electro-mechanical prototypes, fixture-building, and fabrication for active FAB1 projects when shop operations allow.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience in a machine shop, fab shop, or similar environment.

  • Deep working knowledge of mills, lathes, laser cutters, welding, and 3D printing — comfortable both operating and maintaining this equipment.

  • Experience training others on shop equipment and safety procedures, or strong instinct for how to build that kind of program from scratch.

  • Highly organized, with a track record of bringing structure to a space that didn't have it.

  • Comfortable owning a space independently — this role has a lot of autonomy and needs someone who takes initiative rather than waiting for direction.

  • Strong communicator who can set and hold boundaries on safety and access without being a bottleneck.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience managing a shop, lab, or makerspace in an academic, startup, or industrial setting.

  • Background in mechanical design or fabrication (can read drawings, build fixtures, support prototyping).

  • Familiarity with tool/inventory management systems.

  • OSHA or equivalent safety certification experience.

THE ROLE

As our Financial Analyst, you will serve as a core engine for Reframe’s FP&A, operational finance, and strategic planning. You won't just be tracking numbers—you will help define the unit economics of our modular microfactories, track Bill of Materials (BOM) cost reductions, and build financial visibility as we scale from 1 → 10.

This is a high-visibility, high-impact role for a data-driven finance professional who thrives in a fast-paced hardware/manufacturing startup environment.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

1. FP&A & Corporate Financial Modeling

  • Financial Planning & Budgeting: Own and maintain the company’s 3-statement financial model, rolling forecasts, and annual budgeting process.

  • Variance Analysis: Track monthly and quarterly actuals vs. budget (BvA), analyzing key drivers behind revenue, operating expenses, and capex.

  • Executive & Board Reporting: Prepare financial packages, dashboards, and strategic decks for leadership and board meetings.

2. Factory Ops & Unit Economics

  • Cost Accounting & BOM Analysis: Partner with Supply Chain and Manufacturing Engineering to model Bill of Materials (BOM) costs, direct labor rates, and factory overhead absorption.

  • Microfactory Unit Economics: Help analyze and refine the business model for individual microfactories (payback periods, throughput capacity, asset utilization, and gross margin optimization).

  • Capital Allocation: Build ROI models for factory equipment purchases, robotics automation investments, and facility expansion (e.g., FAB1).

3. Cross-Functional Strategic Partnership

  • Departmental Support: Work closely with leaders in Engineering, Software, Factory Operations, and Talent to align headcount planning and operational spend with overall cash runway.

  • Systems & Processes: Help define, select, and implement finance and accounting tooling (ERP integration, spend management, and automated financial reporting).

QULAIFICATIONS

  • Experience: 5-8 years of experience in FP&A, corporate finance, investment banking, management consulting, or startup financial operations.

  • Industry Context: Direct experience or strong familiarity with hardware, manufacturing, robotics, automotive/aerospace, or construction/real estate development finance.

  • Modeling Mastery: Advanced Excel/Google Sheets skills with a proven track record of building dynamic, scalable 3-statement models from scratch.

  • Cost & Operational Acumen: Ability to translate physical operations (BOMs, inventory turns, labor hours, factory throughput) into clear financial metrics and unit economics.

  • Technical & Systems Aptitude: Hands-on experience with modern ERP systems, modern BI/reporting tools, and spend management platforms.

  • Startup Mindset: Scrappy, self-directed, and comfortable operating with ambiguity in a fast-moving physical tech environment.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, or a quantitative field.

  • Experience supporting a hardware or manufacturing company through rapid multi-site scaling.

  • Background working with inventory management, ERP implementation, or supply chain cost-down initiatives.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for a Mechanical Engineering Co-op to join our team at FAB1, our first full-scale microfactory in Billerica, MA, this fall. This role is built for someone who loves the full loop of engineering: sketch it, model it, build it, test it, and fix it — fast. You'll rotate across active projects on our Mechanical Engineering team, working alongside engineers designing the workcells, fixturing, and production infrastructure that make our factory run.

This is a hands-on role. You'll spend real time in the shop — cutting, welding, printing, and machining your own parts — not just handing drawings off to someone else. We move quickly here, so we need someone who can take a rough idea, iterate on it in CAD, get a physical version in hand, and improve it based on what they learn, on a tight timeline.

What You'll Do

  • Design and Iterate Fast: Take on real mechanical design problems across FAB1 projects — fixtures, workstations, material handling, tooling — and move quickly from concept to CAD to working prototype.

  • Build What You Design: Fabricate and assemble your own prototypes and production hardware using mills, lathes, laser cutters, welders, 3D printers, and standard shop tools.

  • Rotate Across Projects: Work across multiple active workstreams on the ME team rather than a single fixed project, picking up context quickly and contributing wherever the team needs hands and ideas.

  • Test and Improve: Validate your designs on the shop floor, troubleshoot what doesn't work, and iterate toward a production-ready result.

  • Support Documentation: Produce clear CAD models and basic technical drawings that a teammate or vendor could build from.

  • Learn the Full Stack: Get exposure to how mechanical design connects to robotics, automation, and factory operations in a live manufacturing environment.

Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a BS in Mechanical Engineering or a related field; junior or senior standing preferred.

  • Solid CAD skills (Onshape, SolidWorks, Fusion 360, or similar) and the ability to go from a rough idea to a modeled part quickly.

  • Comfortable and safe operating shop tools and equipment — mills, lathes, laser cutters, welding, 3D printing, hand and power tools.

  • A fast learner who can pick up new tools, processes, and project context with minimal ramp-up.

  • Bias toward action: you'd rather build a rough prototype and learn from it than perfect a design on paper.

  • Strong communicator who works well within a team and can take direction from multiple engineers across rotating projects.

  • Available for a full-time, semester-length co-op in Billerica, MA this fall.

Nice to Have

  • Prior shop, machine design, or robotics club/competition experience (FSAE, FRC, Baja SAE, etc.).

  • Experience with sheet metal, weldments, or basic structural design.

  • Exposure to manufacturing, construction, or factory automation environments.

  • Familiarity with GD&T fundamentals.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
ABOUT US

Reframe Systems is a Physical AI and robotics company on a mission to make high-performance housing attainable and abundant in the communities where people want to live. We're reimagining the future of housing through a smarter and more sustainable system that empowers people to live better. Come build it with us.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

We are seeking a skilled Drywall Finisher to join our factory team and play a critical role in producing high-quality modular housing components. This role is responsible for taping, mudding, sanding, and finishing drywall seams, joints, corners, and fastener heads to create smooth, market-ready surfaces. The ideal candidate has strong experience with drywall finishing in a manufacturing or production environment, with a commitment to precision, clean work, and production-grade quality that minimizes rework downstream.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Apply joint compound (mud) to drywall seams, joints, and fastener heads using taping knives and appropriate techniques for each coat.

• Tape seams and joints with joint tape, feathering compound edges to create seamless transitions and minimize visible lines.

• Finish corners, both inside and outside, using corner bead and compound to achieve straight, clean lines.

• Sand finished surfaces between coats and prior to final inspection, achieving smooth, defect-free results ready for paint or other finishes.

• Identify and repair imperfections, voids, and damage in drywall panels before mudding begins, coordinating with framers as needed.

• Verify application specifications (fire-rated, moisture-resistant, sound-rated finishes) and apply appropriate finishing techniques for each application.

• Mix, manage, and maintain joint compound at proper consistency to ensure quality application and minimize waste.

• Inspect finished work against specifications and quality standards, addressing touch-ups or rework promptly.

• Work efficiently to meet production schedules while maintaining finish quality standards that reduce or eliminate downstream rework.

• Collaborate with drywall hangers, downstream trades, and supervisors to maintain production flow and handoff standards.

• Communicate with supervisors to address challenges, material issues, and opportunities to improve workflow and efficiency.

• Follow safety protocols, including proper dust containment and respiratory protection in the finishing environment.

• Maintain tools in good condition and keep the work area organized and clean throughout the shift.

QUALIFICATIONS

• High school diploma or equivalent.

• 3+ years of experience finishing drywall, preferably in manufacturing, commercial construction, or production environments.

• Proficiency with drywall finishing techniques that produce smooth, defect-free surfaces ready for paint or final finishes.

• Strong understanding of joint compound types, tape selection, and application methods for different seam conditions.

• Familiarity with tools and equipment used in drywall finishing (e.g., taping knives, mud pans, sanders, corner tools, lifts).

• Ability to read and interpret construction drawings and finish specifications.

• Physical ability to perform tasks including standing for extended periods, working overhead or on ladders, and handling drywall finishing materials and tools.

• Attention to detail and a commitment to craftsmanship and quality output.

• Ability to work efficiently without compromising finish quality.

WORKING CONDITIONS

• Factory environment with exposure to construction materials, tools, joint compound, and dust.

• Physical tasks including standing, reaching overhead, and performing repetitive hand and arm movements.

• Exposure to dust and fumes; proper respiratory protection and ventilation required.

• Some overtime or weekend work may be required based on production schedules.

If you believe you have the skills to thrive in this role, we encourage you to apply—even if you don't meet 100% of the listed requirements. At this time, we are only considering candidates who are authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future visa sponsorship.

  • Give day-to-day direction to receiving and material movement staff and keep the team's daily priorities clear

First 30 days

You know where everything is. You've taken over receiving and daily replenishment, learned our inventory system, and identified the biggest gaps between what the system says and what's on the shelf.

First 90 days

Inventory accuracy is measurably improving. Cycle counting runs on a regular cadence, the kanban system covers our stock items with reorder points you've validated, and production stoppages caused by material handling are rare and documented when they happen.

First year

You've stood up the warehouse and yard at our next facility and made steady-state material flow boring, in the best way: material arrives, gets received same day, and reaches the line without anyone chasing it.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 4+ years in warehouse, inventory, or materials management in a manufacturing or construction environment

  • Hands-on experience with an inventory or ERP system as the person responsible for its accuracy, not just a user

  • Experience with lean replenishment methods (kanban, min/max, cycle counting)

  • Forklift experience; certification a plus, and we'll train and certify you if needed

  • Comfortable working in an active factory and outdoor yard year-round

  • Organized, detail-driven, and willing to own problems end to end

jobs.descriptionHtml:
ABOUT US

Reframe Systems is a Physical AI and robotics company on a mission to make high-performance housing attainable and abundant in the communities where people want to live. Through our vertically integrated delivery model and highly automated microfactories, we deliver climate-resilient homes and buildings with greater speed and predictability than traditional construction.

Our volumetric modular buildings are produced in our Billerica, MA microfactory, with a growing pipeline across North America. We are building a system that balances repeatability with site-responsive design, enabling homes adaptable to each site, community, and customer need. Our cross-disciplinary team brings together architecture, robotics, design engineering, software, factory operations, and field delivery to change how housing gets delivered.

We're reimagining the future of housing through a smarter and more sustainable system that empowers people to live better. Come build it with us.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for a Senior Safety Engineer to own environmental, health, and safety for a factory that builds home modules, and for the field operations that install them on site. Our production mixes automated framing equipment, robotic workcells, CNC processing, overhead lifting, and skilled hand trades working on and around 40-foot modules, with both in-factory and field construction operations.

Our EHS program is young. Station-level hazard assessments, PPE requirements, an emergency action plan, and a training framework are in place, and you'll take over from the teammate who built them. Your job is to foster a company-wide safety culture by turning that foundation into a durable EHS management system that keeps pace with our production ramp. That means taking high-level regulations and “operationalizing” them into standards our employees understand and follow.

This is a hands-on, on-site role for someone who has built a program from the ground up, not inherited a mature one; you'll spend much of your time on the floor, and work closely with production, facilities, and engineering leadership, with the expectation to run the program on modern software tools, not binders.

You don't need to have held an EHS title. If you've built and run compliance programs under heavy external oversight, such as naval nuclear propulsion, aviation maintenance, nuclear power, or pharma and medical device quality, and you know how to operationalize regulations into standards people actually follow, we want to hear from you.

RESPONSIBILTIES

  • Build a safety culture people buy into: clear standards, consistent enforcement, and practical solutions developed with the people doing the work.

  • Operationalize regulatory requirements. Turn OSHA general industry, construction, and environmental standards into clear, practical processes and expectations for every workstation and field task: hazard assessments, work instructions, visual controls, and training that builders can understand and follow without a binder.

  • Own the EHS program and compliance, including recordkeeping, written programs, inspections, and regulatory filings.

  • Maintain hazard assessment and PPE programs for the entire facility, ensuring safe operations grounded in actual requirements.

  • Define and own environmental compliance, including hazardous materials and waste: chemical inventory and SDS management, generator status, waste streams, universal waste, and flammable storage. Partner with facilities to set clear ownership of permits and environmental obligations.

  • Lead safety for high-risk work: working at heights on modules, overhead lifting and rigging, powered industrial trucks, lockout/tagout, machine guarding, and robotic and automated cell safety.

  • Extend the program to field operations at project sites, including coordination with general contractors and other employers on shared sites.

  • Own safety training and certification. Maintain the training matrix, run a train-the-trainer model with internal subject matter experts, and track completion so no one performs a task they aren't qualified for.

  • Formalize stop-work authority and the escalation path behind it, so anyone on the floor or in the field can stop unsafe work without hesitation.

  • Run incident and near-miss reporting, investigation, and corrective action, and close the loop so recurring issues become better standard work.

  • Own emergency preparedness: emergency action plans, drills, fire prevention, and coordination with the local fire department and our insurance carrier's risk engineering team.

  • Put EHS data into the tools the factory already uses, so inspections, corrective actions, and metrics are visible and acted on.

  • Document the program well enough to replicate at future facilities.

30 / 90 / 1 Year Outcomes

First 30 days

You know the floor and the field. You've walked every station, reviewed the existing hazard assessments, written programs, and training records, and built trust with production leads. You've identified the top risks and biggest compliance gaps and have a prioritized plan to close them.

First 90 days

The highest-risk gaps are closed or have scheduled fixes. Incident and near-miss reporting runs through a single system with tracked corrective actions. Training completion is measurable, a regular inspection cadence is in place, and environmental ownership is defined.

First year

EHS runs as a system, not a set of heroics. Stop-work authority is formal and used. Leading indicators are reported and acted on. Hazmat and training programs are audit-ready across factory and field, and the program is documented well enough to stand up at a new site.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 4+ years of EHS experience with direct accountability for a site's safety and compliance program OR

  • 4+ years managing externally regulated compliance programs in mature industries (military, nuclear, aviation, pharma/medical device, aerospace, or similar). This experience must also be augmented with additional time in scaling enterprises.

  • Has built or substantially stood up a program in a new facility, a new organization, or a rapidly scaling operation.

  • A track record of operationalizing regulations: you can take a standard written at a high level and turn it into something a crew member can act on during a shift.

  • Working knowledge of OSHA general industry standards, or the ability to get there quickly; construction standards a plus.

  • Experience with hazardous materials, chemical safety, or waste compliance.

  • Experience managing safety for field or construction crews is a strong plus

  • Comfortable running a program on digital tools and quick to adopt new software.

  • Credible on the floor: you can set a standard, explain why it matters, and hold the line respectfully.

  • Professional certification (CSP, ASP, CHST, CHMM, or similar) is a plus

  • On-site in Billerica, MA, 5 days/week, with travel to field sites as needed

jobs.descriptionHtml:
ABOUT US

Reframe Systems is a Physical AI and robotics company on a mission to make high-performance housing attainable and abundant in the communities where people want to live. Through our vertically integrated delivery model and highly automated microfactories, we deliver climate resilient homes and buildings with greater speed and predictability than traditional construction.

Our volumetric modular buildings are produced in our Andover, MA microfactory, with a growing pipeline across North America and a new microfactory on the way. We are building a system that balances repeatability with site-responsive design, enabling homes that are adaptable to each site, community, and customer need. Our cross-disciplinary team brings together architecture, robotics, design engineering, software, factory operations, and field delivery to change how housing gets delivered.

We’re reimagining the future of housing through a smarter and more sustainable system that empowers people to live better. Come build it with us.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Your mission is to help build the next generation of our Pixels-to-Parts system: the software that turns a design, a floor plan and configurations, into every part our microfactory needs to build a home. Here's a somewhat recent talk from Ethan Keller, the tech lead for the Pixels-to-Parts team, showing what the system can do (as of Nov 2025):

We are seeking a software engineer to build the agentic workflows that interpret intent and the deterministic code that turns a design into exact geometry, parts and visualizations. You don't need CAD or architecture experience; we'd rather you question decades-old assumptions about design software and rebuild the stack from first principles, learning the domain alongside people who know buildings and manufacturing well. If you're a strong generalist who enjoys breaking down fuzzy problems, shipping, and seeing your code have real world impact (in this case, houses and apartments), this is your platform.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Help architect and build the core of our design automation platform: turn a floor plan into manufacturing-ready building design.

  • Turn our building system’s design decisions into a library of programmatic checks. Each one validates a model against hard dimensional, code and manufacturing constraints, and explains a failure by pointing to the rule behind it.

  • Build agentic workflows: tool-using agents, MCP servers, and retrieval over our design and product data

  • Develop evals and guardrails that check model outputs against hard physical, code and manufacturing constraints

  • Write deterministic, well-tested code that generates geometry, parts lists and manufacturing data from a design

  • Help build the visualization layer so designers, customers and the factory can see and verify a design

  • Deploy and operate what you build in the cloud: containers, infrastructure as code, CI/CD and observability

  • Work closely with Architecture, Design Engineering, DFMA (design for manufacturing and assembly) and Factory Operations. Learn how buildings are designed and built, including on the factory floor.

  • Improve our engineering practices, tooling and developer experience as the team grows

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related quantitative field is preferred; equivalent experience is welcome

  • 5+ years building production software, with Python as a primary language

  • Experience shipping cloud-native software (containers, managed services, infrastructure as code, CI/CD)

  • Strong interest in agentic systems, shown through work or side projects, e.g., MCP servers, RAG pipelines, LangGraph or similar frameworks, tool-calling agents, LLM evals. Production experience is a significant plus

  • Comfort with the math and algorithms behind your code (geometry, linear algebra, graphs or optimization)

  • A generalist's range: comfortable moving between backend, data, infrastructure and some frontend as the problem requires

  • Experience setting technical direction for a system or team

  • Track record of mentoring engineers and raising the bar on engineering practices.

  • Ability to navigate ambiguity. You work effectively under deadlines and shifting priorities while maintaining quality and accountability

  • Clear written and verbal communication, and a hands-on, "no fences" approach to collaboration

  • Able to work on-site in Billerica, MA at least 2 days a week

  • Bonus: Exposure to manufacturing, robotics, hardware or other systems where software meets the physical world is a plus. No CAD, BIM or architecture experience required

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We are seeking a Licensed Plumber (Class 2) to join our team and play a critical role across both factory and field operations. This dynamic position offers the opportunity to work in a controlled factory environment to assemble modular housing systems and participate in on-site plumbing installations during project builds. You will also contribute to the design process, providing valuable input on plumbing layouts and constructability. The ideal candidate is technically skilled, detail-oriented, and motivated to grow their career.

RESPOPNSIBILTIES

  • Perform plumbing installations in modular housing units, including water supply lines, drainage systems, and gas piping.

  • Complete on-site plumbing connections during module installations, ensuring compliance with all codes and project specifications.

  • Work closely with engineers and designers to review plumbing layouts and provide input on system specifications and constructability.

  • Contribute to the development of shop drawings and ensure alignment with the Massachusetts Plumbing Code.

  • Collaborate with production teams, field crews, and other trades to complete projects on time and with precision.

  • Supervise and mentor apprentices, providing guidance and fostering skill development.

  • Ensure all plumbing work adheres to Massachusetts Plumbing Code and Reframe Systems’ standards.

  • Conduct quality checks to verify system integrity and functionality.

  • Maintain a clean and organized workspace, following all safety protocols.

  • Diagnose and resolve plumbing issues in both factory and field environments.

  • Communicate effectively with supervisors to address challenges and propose solutions.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Valid Massachusetts Licensed Plumber (Class 2) license.

  • 3+ years of experience as a licensed plumber, preferably in manufacturing, modular construction, or commercial/residential projects.

  • Strong knowledge of plumbing codes and standards, particularly the Massachusetts Plumbing Code.

  • Proficiency in plumbing tools, equipment, and testing devices.

  • Experience reading and interpreting blueprints, diagrams, and digital plans.

  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work overhead, and perform tasks requiring manual dexterity.

  • Excellent communication and problem-solving skills.

CAREER GROWTH OPPORTUNITIES

You will have access to a pathway to achieve your Master Plumber (Class 1) license, including:

  • Tuition reimbursement for Board-approved courses.

  • Flexible scheduling for education and exam preparation.

  • Financial support for exam and licensure fees.

  • Leadership opportunities and expanded responsibilities upon licensure.

Reframe is building something real, in a physical space, with a workforce that is growing fast. The people function here is not administrative overhead — it's operational infrastructure. You'll have real ownership, real visibility, and real impact from day one.
